Globus’s narrower portfolio in these segments leaves it vulnerable to bundle pricing and cross-selling advantages wielded by larger competitors.
3. **Procedural Standard-of-Care Inertia:** Despite technological advancements, open surgery continues to hold the largest market share in 2026 due to widespread surgeon familiarity, established clinical protocols, and applicability to complex cases [9]. This creates a structural barrier to robotic/enabling technology adoption unless Globus can consistently demonstrate superior outcomes or cost efficiencies.
4. **Agile & Regional Competitors:** Beyond the giants, Globus faces pressure from specialized and regional players like Arthrex, VB Spine, Orthofix, and Integra LifeSciences, which can compete on niche innovation, speed-to-market, or surgical preference alignment [7], [8], [9].

Globus Medical occupies a defensible #2 position in spine surgery with an increasingly integrated ecosystem moat, but its long-term durability hinges on execution precision rather than strategic vision alone.
